newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Discovery says forms new oil alliance.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Discovery says forms new oil alliance.

text.p: Discovery Petroleum NL said on Friday it has formed an alliance with Phoenix Energy Pty Ltd to carry out an extensive exploration and development programme in the northern Perth Basin, onshore Western Australia.
The joint effort will include up to nine exploration wells and at least one development well in the Mount Horner oil field over a three-year period, Discovery said.

Discovery, currently the target of an A$0.80 cents a share takeover bid worth A$104.2 million by Premier Oil Plc of Britain, said the location of the wells will be selected following a geological study.
Phoenix is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Griffin Group, whose main assets in Australia is the unlisted Griffin Coal Mining Co Pty Ltd.
wells will be drilled for both oil and gas over a range of depths, Discovery said.
Phoenix can earn up to a half share in of all Discovery's exploration interests in the Basin by contributing up to A$13 million to exploration, Discovery said.
A 50 percent interin Discovery's Mount Horner oil field is included in the earning structure, Discovery said.
Total spending by both parties could run up to A$19 million, Discovery said.
Premier, has denied claims by some analysts that it was less interested in Discovery's older Australian assets than in its newer Indonesian holdings in Kakap region, near some of its own properties.
Discovery continues to be the focus of speculation that it will soon attract a rival bid by Oil Search Ltd, whose main assets are in Papua New Guinea.
Oil Search in late September paid A$0.75 a share for a 10.1 percent stake in Discovery.
Analysts have suggested a rival bid of between A$0.82 and A$0.86 may be required to clinch a takeover.
Oil Search has said little more than that a takeover of Discovery is one option the company is exploring.
Discovery shares ended unchanged at A$0.82.
